page.layout: One page of text in a single column; a running head with page number at top right; below the text, a small calculation (division scheme) with numbers in columns, and a catchword-like mark "C" at bottom right, which is a printer's or reader's mark and not a catchword.

main_text.p: Hic Denominatores multiplico, dicens: quater 5 sunt 20, & quinquies 20 sunt 100, quæ seorsim noto.
Nunc 2 subjectis centum, & multiplicatis exurgunt 200, quæ divido per 5, & proveniunt 40.
Deinde 3 subjectis centum, & multiplicatis exurgunt 200, quæ divido per 4, & existunt 75.
Tertiò 4 subnotatis centum, & multiplicatis, exurgunt 300, quæ divido per 5, & habeo 80.
Iam per additionem numeris in unam summam collectis dico, 195 lucrati sunt 288 aureos. Quot lucrantur 40? Deinde quot lucrantur 75? tertiò quot lucrantur 80? Et semper secundum Regulam Detri operor.

page.notes: The scan shows a worked division example in the printed Latin text, with fractions 2/5, 3/4, 4/5 set above the columns. The fractions and the computation grid are rendered in plain text as best as possible; the layout of the sums (dividing 200 by 5, 300 by 4, 400 by 5, and the addition 40+75+80=195) is reproduced as printed. The final figure "288" in the text and the sum "195" in the grid are printed as they appear. The small mark "C" at bottom right is not transcribed as text.
